examples.text: The film occupied three hours of my time.

I corralled the judge, and we started off across the fields, in no very mild state of fear of that gentleman's wife, whose vigilance was seldom relaxed. And thus we came by a circuitous route to Mohair, the judge occupied by his own guilty thoughts, and I by others not less disturbing.

glosses: To possess or use the time or capacity of; to engage the service of.

examples.text: The film occupied me for three hours.
I occupy myself with gardening for a few hours every day.

glosses: To fill or hold (an official position or role).

examples.text: I occupy the post of deputy cat catcher.
I occupied her friend while he made his proposal.
The historic mansion occupied two city blocks.
The better apartments were already occupied.

With fresh material, taxonomic conclusions are leavened by recognition that the material examined reflects the site it occupied; a herbarium packet gives one only a small fraction of the data desirable for sound conclusions. Herbarium material does not, indeed, allow one to extrapolate safely: what you see is what you get[…]

glosses: To have, or to have taken, possession or control of (a territory).

examples.text: The Japanese can occupy but cannot hold, and what they can hold they cannot hold long, was the opinion of General Pai Chung-hsi, Chief of the General Staff of the Chinese Army, […]

glosses: To place the theodolite or total station at (a point).

1867, Robert Nares A Glossary
OCCUPY, [sensu obsc.] To possess, or enjoy.
These villains will make the word captain, as odious as the word occupy. 2 Hen. IV, ii, 4.
Groyne, come of age, his state sold out of hand
For 's whore; Groyne still doth occupy his land. B. Jons. Epigr., 117.
Many, out of their own obscene apprehensions, refuse proper and fit words, as occupy, nature, and the like. Ibid., Discoveries, vol. vii, p. 119.
It is so used also in Rowley's New Wonder, Anc. Dr., v, 278.

glosses: To do business in; to busy oneself with.

examples.text: All the ships of the sea, with their mariners, were in thee to occupy the merchandise.

glosses: To use; to expend; to make use of.
